newsitem.title: USA: Republic Industries to acquire New Jersey car dealers.
newsitem.headline: Republic Industries to acquire New Jersey car dealers.

text.p: Republic Industries Inc., the diversified company that recently bought National Car Rental Systems Inc., said Wednesday it agreed to acquire two New Jersey-based car dealerships for $55 million in stock.
Following the news, Republic Industries' stock rose $1.25 to $35 in active trading on Nasdaq.
Republic, which also has stakes in solid waste and electronic security services, said it would acquire Flemington Car and Truck Country and Princeton's Nassau Conover's dealerships.

The Fort Lauderdale, Fla.-based company has been acquiring car dealerships recently. Last month, it announced the acquisition of Taylor Jeep-Eagle Inc. in Detroit and Champion Chevrolet Co. in Los Angeles in exchange for $20 million in Republic stock.
It also bought Courtesy Auto Group Inc., which has dealerships in Orlando, Fla., in another stock deal worth $30 million.
In late February, Republic acquired National Car Rental, which operates a fleet of 100,000 vehicles in North America and overseas, in exchange for 27 million shares of its common stock.
